items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 9 at 1:34PM PST until November 10 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Minor to locally moderate coastal flooding during morning
high tides, as well as dangerous rip currents and breaking waves
due to elevated surf up to 5 to 8 feet expected, especially
across west facing beaches.

* WHERE...Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide at
beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with normal tidal
ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 7.2 to 7.4 feet (MLLW) are
expected each morning. Surf and coastal flooding impacts peak on
Monday. Since the large swell is from the west, south facing
areas such as Long Beach will be less affected unlike the
previous events where the swell was from the south.
items.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.
